reason: GO-2026-6443 merges the 1.84 and 1.85 development lines into one range, [1.84.0-dev, 1.85.0-dev.0.20260825072537-93e31b48545e), so every 1.84 release matches. The fix landed on the 1.84 line at d5a41119e0e3 (v1.84.0-dev.0.20260825144003-d5a41119e0e3), which is an ancestor of the v1.84.0 tag (e84aa5ab15d1). GHSA-2v4p-qf9q-27wj, the same vulnerability, records the two lines separately and treats v1.84.0 as fixed. The override covers only released 1.84.x; 1.84.0-dev and 1.85.0-dev pseudo-versions before their fixes stay affected.

GO-2026-5932 marks the golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package as unmaintained and unsafe by design. It names no fixed version, so it matches every x/crypto release, but it affects only code that imports x/crypto/openpgp. The bundle keeps the module and drops the package list, so a module-level match cannot tell an openpgp importer from anyone else. Reported as a notice, not a vulnerability.
